attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. He cites Schmidhuber nearby, but this sentence is his own assertion.

semantics.note: Accurate on Fukushima, Zhang's 1988 back-propagation work and priority over LeCun. It leaves out the Japanese-with-English-abstract detail, but the contract puts that back as its own commitment.

contract.note: The criteria follow his words: dates, Zhang's use of back-propagation, the publication language and abstract, and priority over LeCun's earliest qualifying work. This is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Fukushima's 2019 paper classes the neocognitron as a CNN first proposed in 1979 and cites the 1979 and 1980 papers. It is his own account but well dated. Supports the Fukushima part.

English translation of the September 1988 JSAP entry, describing back-propagation on a simplified neocognitron with space-invariant connections. Supports the 1988 back-propagation part. Because it is a translation, it does not show an original English abstract.
LeCun's 1989 NIPS paper is a later comparison point. It does not date his earliest qualifying work, so it cannot settle who was first.

reviews.rationale: The Fukushima part and Zhang's 1988 use of back-propagation are supported. The original English abstract was not checked, and LeCun's earliest qualifying work is not dated, so the priority claim is open. Nothing in the packet contradicts any part. The support condition needs every part, so the claim as a whole is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical statement in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'only when' timing and the qualifier 'sharply, publicly critical'. It is correctly treated as a claim about when the criticism began, not why.

contract.note: Treating a categorical public critique published before ChatGPT launched as a counterexample is a fair, ordinary reading. It does not need an exact date for when ChatGPT eclipsed Meta.

evidence.note: Noema essay co-written by LeCun, dated 23 Aug 2022. It discusses LLMs and says text-only systems will never approximate human understanding. That is sharp, public and categorical, and it predates ChatGPT.
OpenAI's own announcement dates ChatGPT's launch to 30 Nov 2022. It is a company disclosure, used only for the date.

reviews.rationale: LeCun co-wrote a public, categorical criticism of LLMs in August 2022, more than three months before ChatGPT launched. ChatGPT could not have eclipsed Meta before it existed, so LeCun's sharp public criticism did not begin only after that.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Matches both negative claims: LeCun did not invent CNNs, and he was not the first to train their weights with back-propagation.

contract.note: The back-propagation result depends on counting TDNN, a 1-D network that shares weights over time, as a CNN. Marcus says TDNN 'presaged' CNNs with the same math, but counting it is a common informed reading. Without it, Zhang (Sept 1988) against LeCun (1988) would be open.

evidence.note: Fukushima dates the neocognitron, which he classes as a CNN, to 1979. LeCun began later. Supports the 'did not invent' part.
Waibel's ATR report of October 1987 describes back-propagation training with weights shared across time shifts, so a back-propagation-trained 1-D convolutional network existed in 1987.
A reproduced interview in which LeCun says he began shared-weight experiments in 1988. That is after Waibel's 1987 report. It is a retrospective self-account, and the reproduction is dated.

reviews.rationale: The neocognitron (1979) came before LeCun's CNN work. Under the contract's broad meaning of CNN, Waibel's 1987 TDNN used back-propagation with shared weights before LeCun's 1988 start. Nothing in the packet shows LeCun was first at either. The result depends on counting TDNN as a CNN.
